name: EPCRA Tier II hazardous chemical inventory reporting thresholds by state
description: The quantity threshold at which a facility must file an annual Tier II hazardous chemical inventory report in each US state, compared to the federal EPCRA Section 312 baseline. Federal thresholds: ≥10,000 lbs for hazardous chemicals, ≥500 lbs or the threshold planning quantity (whichever is lower) for extremely hazardous substances (40 CFR Part 370). EPA authorizes states to set lower thresholds and add chemicals, and at least 9 states have done so: California (55 gal/500 lbs), Louisiana (500 lbs), Vermont (100 lbs — among the strictest), Delaware (55 gal/500 lbs), Oregon (dual-level system), Nevada (IFC-based, some categories at 0 lbs), Alaska (any quantity for certain hazard classes), New Jersey (own EHS list), and New York City (own EHS list with very low thresholds). Answers 'does my California facility need to file Tier II for 600 pounds of a hazardous chemical' (yes — California threshold is 500 lbs, below the federal 10,000), 'what is Nevada's reporting threshold for flammable materials', and 'which states have lower Tier II thresholds than federal'.
licence: Federal regulations are US Government works, not copyrightable. State regulations are state government works. Facts are not copyrightable (Feist, 1991); each record quotes a short attributed span and links back.

records.special_categories: any quantity of a hazardous material identified in federal placarding regulations: Poison Gas Hazard Division 2.3 and Poisons 6.1, Explosives 1.1, 1.2 and 1.3 (excluding smokeless gunpowder, black powder, and ammunition), Flammable Solid Divisions 4.1, 4.2 and 4.3, and Radioactive Hazard Class 7. Additionally, any compressed gas must be reported at ≥1,000 cubic feet
records.source_quote: Alaska, the lower thresholds apply to any quantity of a hazardous material identified in federal placarding regulations: Poison Gas Hazard Division 2.3 and Poisons 6.1, Explosives 1.1, 1.2 and 1.3 (excluding smokeless gunpowder, black powder, and ammunition), Flammable Solid Divisions 4.1, 4.2 and 4.3, and Radioactive Hazard Class 7. Additionally, any compressed gas must be reported at ≥1,000 cubic feet.

California, the hazardous materials report is called a Hazardous Materials Business Plan and is significantly more in-depth than a standard Tier II report. The reporting thresholds for California are: 55 gallons (liquids) 500 pounds (solids) 200 cubic feet (compressed gasses) Any quantity of hazardous waste

records.special_categories: Requires use of Tier2 Submit. The state distributes reports to LEPCs and fire departments that maintain the same reporting requirements
records.source_quote: Colorado: Requires use of Tier2 Submit. The state distributes reports to LEPCs and fire departments that maintain the same reporting requirements. Some LEPCs and fire departments may require additional reporting elements.

records.special_categories: Requires Tier II reports to be submitted directly to local fire departments, often with unique local formatting and mapping requirements
records.source_quote: Connecticut: Requires Tier II reports to be submitted directly to local fire departments, often with unique local formatting and mapping requirements.

records.general_threshold: 55 gallons or 500 pounds for hazardous materials, whichever is lower, unless the Threshold Planning Quantity (TPQ) is lowest
records.special_categories: The only chemicals with a 10,000-pound threshold are those which are used exclusively for heating the facility
records.source_quote: Delaware, the reporting threshold is 55 gallons or 500 pounds for hazardous materials, whichever is lower, unless the Threshold Planning Quantity (TPQ) is lowest, in which case it must be used. The only chemicals with a 10,000-pound threshold are those which are used exclusively for heating the facility.

records.ehs_threshold: 500 pounds (227 kg—approximately 55 gallons) or the Threshold Planning Quantity (TPQ), whichever is lower
records.source_quote: A hazardous chemical that is an Extremely Hazardous Substance (EHS) is present at your facility at any one time in an amount equal to or greater than 500 pounds (227 kg—approximately 55 gallons) or the Threshold Planning Quantity (TPQ), whichever is lower. EHSs and their TPQs are listed in Appendices A and B of <https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-40/part-355> 40 CFR part 355 . ( 2 ) A hazardous chemical that is not an EHS is present at your facility at any one time in an amount equal to or greater than the threshold level for that hazardous chemical. Threshold levels for such hazardous chemicals are: ( i ) For any hazardous chemical that does not meet the criteria in <https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-40/section-370.10#p-370.10(a)(2)(ii)> paragraph (a)(2)(ii) or <https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-40/section-370.10#p-370.10(a)(2)(iii)> (iii) of this section, the threshold level is 10,000 pounds (or 4,540 kg).

records.special_categories: Accepts Tier II reports through E-Plan and imposes additional requirements related to facility emergency contacts and notifications
records.source_quote: Florida: Accepts Tier II reports through E-Plan and imposes additional requirements related to facility emergency contacts and notifications.

records.special_categories: Uses the state-managed SERC portal with specific formatting expectations for site maps
records.source_quote: Illinois: Uses the state-managed SERC portal with specific formatting expectations for site maps.

records.general_threshold: 500 pounds for any hazardous materials unless the Threshold Planning Quantity (TPQ) is lower
records.special_categories: used oil must also be reported
records.source_quote: Louisiana, the reporting threshold is 500 pounds for any hazardous materials unless the Threshold Planning Quantity (TPQ) is lower, in which case it must be used. In addition to the lower threshold, used oil must also be reported.

records.general_threshold: determined using the International Fire Code List (IFC). The different material types range from flammable materials to water-reactive materials and have thresholds ranging from 0 to 500 lbs
records.special_categories: no exemptions can be applied to a material that falls into one of the IFC categories. However, if a chemical does not apply to one of the IFC categories, then it follows Federal Tier II thresholds and federal exemptions apply
records.source_quote: Nevada, the hazardous material storage report is called the Community Right-to-Know Act. The reporting thresholds in Nevada are determined using the International Fire Code List (IFC). The different material types range from flammable materials to water-reactive materials and have thresholds ranging from 0 to 500 lbs. Also, no exemptions can be applied to a material that falls into one of the IFC categories. However, if a chemical does not apply to one of the IFC categories, then it follows Federal Tier II thresholds and federal exemptions apply.

records.special_categories: relies on International Fire Code (IFC) thresholds rather than the federal 10,000-pound standard, often triggering reporting at much lower quantities for common chemicals
records.source_quote: Nevada (Clark County): Tier II reporting differs from most states because it relies on International Fire Code (IFC) thresholds rather than the federal 10,000-pound standard, often triggering reporting at much lower quantities for common chemicals.

records.ehs_threshold: its own EHS list to determine the chemical-specific reporting threshold
records.special_categories: any facility that does not have a covered NAICS Code is exempt from reporting
records.source_quote: New Jersey – The hazardous material storage report for New Jersey is referred to as the Community Right to Know Program. New Jersey has instated its own EHS list to determine the chemical-specific reporting threshold. The list is also substantially larger than the federal list and includes a number of solids it has deemed “unusually hazardous substances.” Additionally, the state has a NAICS Code assessment and any facility that does not have a covered NAICS Code is exempt from reporting.

records.special_categories: State agencies accept Tier II reports via E-Plan
records.source_quote: New York: State agencies accept Tier II reports via E-Plan.

records.ehs_threshold: its own EHS list with very low reporting thresholds
records.special_categories: if the CAS number is on the NYC EHS list and is stored over the threshold, it must be reported. However, if not on the list, federal thresholds apply
records.source_quote: New York City is also referred to as the Community Right-to-Know Program and must be completed in addition to the New York state report. New York City has its own EHS list with very low reporting thresholds. For any pure substance, if the CAS number is on the NYC EHS list and is stored over the threshold, it must be reported. However, if not on the list, federal thresholds apply.

records.general_threshold: Upper Reporting Levels (URL): 500 gallons (liquids) 500 pounds (solids) 500 cubic feet (non-liquefied gases) 500 gallons (liquefied gases)
records.special_categories: Substances that are highly toxic or explosive apply to the Lower Reporting Levels (LRL). 5 gallons (liquids) 10 pounds (solids) 20 cubic feet (compressed gasses) Non-sealed radioactive: reportable at any amount
records.source_quote: Oregon are determined using a dual-level reporting system. Substances that are highly toxic or explosive apply to the Lower Reporting Levels (LRL). 5 gallons (liquids) 10 pounds (solids) 20 cubic feet (compressed gasses) Non-sealed radioactive: reportable at any amount All other substances must adhere to the Upper Reporting Levels (URL): 500 gallons (liquids) 500 pounds (solids) 500 cubic feet (non-liquefied gases) 500 gallons (liquefied gases)

records.special_categories: Requires exclusive use of E-Plan for state submissions
records.source_quote: South Carolina: Requires exclusive use of E-Plan for state submissions.

records.special_categories: All facilities must submit using the STEERS Tier II Reporting system
records.source_quote: Texas: All facilities must submit using the STEERS Tier II Reporting system.

records.general_threshold: 100 pounds or the TPQ, whichever is lower
records.ehs_threshold: 100 pounds or the TPQ, whichever is lower
records.special_categories: For all petroleum products and fuels, the threshold is ≥10,000 lbs Carcinogens must be reported at any amount Explosives must be reported at any amount
records.source_quote: Vermont, the state-specific reporting thresholds are as follows: For all EHSs, as well as all other hazardous chemicals or substances and pesticides for which an SDS is required, the threshold is 100 pounds or the TPQ, whichever is lower. For all petroleum products and fuels, the threshold is ≥10,000 lbs Carcinogens must be reported at any amount Explosives must be reported at any amount
